title: Can the Free World Still Build?
description: Housing, grids, transit, factories and defense production increasingly reveal the same failure: wealthy democracies that struggle to execute.
question: Can open societies recover speed and scale without weakening law, consent or restraint?

title: Who Controls Intelligence?
description: Frontier AI depends on concentrated chips, compute, models and distribution, giving a small number of firms and states extraordinary power.
question: Can intelligence remain open without becoming dangerously concentrated or dangerously available?

title: China's Manufacturing State
description: China has turned supplier density, production learning and industrial scale into strategic power while the West has lost industrial depth.
question: Can market democracies rebuild strategic industry without becoming command economies?

title: The New Arsenal
subtitle: Drones, autonomy and the end of expensive war
description: Cheap drones, autonomous systems and software are rewriting the economics of war faster than Western procurement can adapt.
question: Can democratic militaries move at software speed while preserving human responsibility?

title: Can Democracy Survive Synthetic Reality?
description: AI can fabricate any voice, image or document, and make genuine evidence easier to dismiss.
question: Can societies authenticate reality without creating an authority that decides what is real?

title: Europe After the American Guarantee
description: Europe has wealth, technology and military experience, but fragmented industry and decades of dependence have limited its strategic agency.
question: Can Europe defend itself without weakening the alliance that has protected it?

title: AI Needs Electricity
subtitle: The return of energy abundance
description: Data centres, industry, electrification and defense production are converging on one constraint: reliable power at enormous scale.
question: Can the free world build the energy system technological leadership requires?

title: The Demographic Winter
description: Falling fertility and aging are reshaping growth, public finance, migration, military recruitment and confidence in the future.
question: Can a civilization remain dynamic when each generation is smaller than the last?

title: Borders, Belonging and Democratic Consent
description: Immigration can renew aging societies and deepen prosperity, but only where states can control entry, build capacity and sustain belonging.
question: How open can a society remain without losing the consent that makes openness possible?

title: The Authoritarian Network
description: China, Russia, Iran and North Korea increasingly reinforce one another across weapons, energy, finance, technology and diplomacy.
question: Are open societies facing separate adversaries, or a connected strategic system?

title: Can Democracy Act Without a Strongman?
description: When institutions repeatedly fail to deliver, concentrated power begins to look less like tyranny and more like competence.
question: Can democracy act decisively without making power harder to restrain or reverse?

title: Can Capitalism Still Legitimate Itself?
description: Markets remain the engine of prosperity, but scarcity, rent extraction and concentrated ownership are weakening public consent.
question: Can capitalism recover broad legitimacy without sacrificing dynamism?

title: The Meritocracy Crisis
description: Open societies need demanding standards, and credible pathways through which talent can rise.
question: Can merit remain real without becoming inherited, performative or politically allocated?

title: When Intelligence Becomes Cheap
subtitle: AI and the end of the white-collar bargain
description: AI may remove the junior work through which professionals learn, advance and build judgment.
question: What happens to education, work and status when cognitive skill is no longer scarce?

title: The State Can No Longer Afford Itself
titleHtml: The State Can No Longer Afford Itself
description: Pensions, healthcare, defense, industrial policy, infrastructure and climate adaptation are colliding with debt and weak growth.
question: Can democracies choose among worthy priorities before crisis chooses for them?

title: Trade After Trust
description: Export controls, tariffs, subsidies and friend-shoring are replacing a trade system built around efficiency with one organized around security.
question: What should remain global when economic interdependence can be weaponized?

title: Financial Chokepoints and the Future of Money
titleHtml: Financial Chokepoints and the Future of Money
description: Sanctions, reserve currencies, payment rails and stablecoins are turning financial infrastructure into a battlefield of state power.
question: How long can the open world weaponize its networks before others build credible alternatives?

title: The Elements of Power
subtitle: Critical minerals and the physical limits of sovereignty
description: Batteries, grids, chips and weapons depend on mineral processing concentrated in a small number of countries.
question: Can democracies secure the materials they need without abandoning environmental and labor standards?

title: The Chip Order
description: Advanced semiconductors rely on a fragile, highly concentrated chain of design tools, equipment, fabrication, packaging and talent.
question: Can open societies protect a strategic chokepoint without fragmenting the innovation system that created it?

title: The Robot Economy
description: AI is acquiring a body, bringing automation into factories, logistics, vehicles, care and the home.
question: Will embodied intelligence restore productivity and industrial capacity, or concentrate power and displace work?

title: Biology Becomes Programmable
description: Gene editing, protein design and automated laboratories are turning living systems into an engineering medium.
question: Can open science unlock biology's benefits without making catastrophic capabilities widely accessible?

title: The Surveillance Bargain
description: Digital identity, biometrics, data brokers and AI administration promise safer, more efficient societies at the cost of deeper visibility into individual life.
question: How much privacy can an open society surrender before freedom becomes mostly formal?

title: The Digital Sovereignty State
description: Clouds, data, platforms, models and digital identity are being reorganized around borders and strategic control.
question: Can democracies reduce technological dependency without closing the internet or expanding state power?

title: The Space Infrastructure of Sovereignty
description: Communications, navigation, financial timing, intelligence and warfare increasingly depend on privately operated systems in orbit.
question: Who should control infrastructure on which sovereign states can no longer function without?

title: The New Nuclear Age
description: More nuclear actors, weaker arms control and the entanglement of AI, cyber and space systems are making deterrence less legible.
question: Can open societies preserve strategic stability when decision time is shrinking and uncertainty is growing?

title: The World After the UN
description: Institutions built for 1945 are struggling to act in a world of vetoes, rival blocs and transnational threats.
question: Should the free world keep reforming universal institutions, or build smaller coalitions that can decide and act?

title: The World That Will Not Choose Sides
titleHtml: The World That Will Not Choose Sides
subtitle: India, the Gulf and the rise of strategic middle powers
description: India, the Gulf, Turkey, Indonesia and other middle powers are pursuing flexible partnerships rather than permanent alignment.
question: Can open societies build durable partnerships with states that share interests but not all of their values?

title: Climate Adaptation Is State Capacity
description: Heat, fire, flood, water stress and insurance withdrawal are turning climate risk into a test of housing, infrastructure and public competence.
question: Can democracies protect people from unavoidable risk without abandoning mitigation or honest pricing?

title: Can Liberalism Produce Loyalty?
description: Rights and procedures protect pluralism, but may not by themselves generate solidarity, duty or sacrifice.
question: Can an open society cultivate common purpose without coercion, exclusion or manufactured nationalism?

title: Why the Future Stopped Feeling Better
description: Advanced societies still invent, but increasingly fail to translate invention into affordable housing, better services, higher productivity and confidence.
question: What would make progress visible, and believable, again?
